isis_nephthys_kneeling.name: Nephthys and Isis

descriptions.default: Nephthys and Isis kneel side by side, their name signs on their heads: the basket on a house for Nephthys, the throne for Isis.

isis_nephthys_kneeling.reference: TBP Spruch 17 (lists the Nephthys sign and the throne sign among this vignette's motifs)

nut_over_scarab.name: Nut

descriptions.default: A goddess, probably Nut, the sky, bends low over a lying lion and a scarab: the sun, soon to be born again from her body.

nut_over_scarab.reference: that the goddess is Nut is unsourced

descriptions.default: Osiris sits on his throne in the tall atef crown, holding his sceptre, as the dead man comes before him.
A tall stand with a round loaf and a lotus flower, set before Osiris.
The dead man raises his hands in praise before Osiris.
Anubis, the jackal-headed god of embalming, stands behind the dead man as he worships Osiris.
A man carries a chest high on one hand. It may be the funeral chest "containing the bowels of Osiris", which Anubis guards.
Nephthys and Isis raise a hand toward the boat; Isis holds an ankh. "Isis cast away his impurities, Nephthys cut off his sins."
Two baboons stand upright and raise their paws in praise of the sun in its boat.
A god crowned with the sun disc sits in his boat before a stand with a lotus. He is probably Atum, the evening sun, who in the text "built thy house" and crosses to the eastern horizon.
Two baboons stand upright and raise their paws in praise of the sun in its boat.
Isis and Nephthys stand with a hand raised, each holding an ankh. The dead man "was conceived by Isis, begotten by Nephthys."
Two baboons squat on their haunches, greeting the sun.
Khepri, the rising sun, rides in his boat. "O Chepera in his bark! ... Chepera in his bark is Harmachis himself."
The heading of the chapter continues: "May the living soul of the Osiris N be, among the devotees, near the great company of the gods in the Amenti, after the burying."
The dead man kneels with both hands raised before Khepri's boat.

two_apes_isis_nephthys.name: Two apes

descriptions.default: Two baboons squat facing the boat of the rising sun. They may stand for Isis and Nephthys: the text names the "reckoners" whom Khepri in his bark empowers as the baboon, Isis and Nephthys.

two_apes_isis_nephthys.reference: TBP Spruch 17 (Backes: the Abrechner are the baboon, Isis and Nephthys); Davis 1894 ("the two girls")

falcon_on_standard.name: Falcon on a standard

descriptions.default: A falcon perches on a tall standard, a flail at its back. It looks like the sign for the West, but why it stands here is not known. The dead man "flies away like a hawk."

falcon_on_standard.reference: Davis 1894; "the sign for the West" is unsourced

great_cat_and_apep.name: The great cat

descriptions.default: "I am this great cat who frequenteth the Persea tree in Heliopolis." The cat is Ra himself, holding down the snake, the enemy of the sun, on the night of battle.

great_cat_and_apep.reference: Davis 1894; Lucarelli 2022 (reads the cat as Atum, the snake as Apophis)

descriptions.default: The sacred persea tree of Heliopolis, where the great cat fights the snake.
A small figure with a beaked head sits beside the tree with one knee drawn up. Who it is is not known.

twin_souls.name: The twin souls

descriptions.default: Two bearded gods sit on thrones: Osiris and Ra. Osiris enters Djedu and meets the soul of Ra there, and "the soul of the one embraces the soul of the other."

twin_souls.reference: Davis 1894; Stadler 2022 reads Mendes for Djedu

descriptions.default: Two ribbed bowls stand side by side with signs heaped on them. What they show is not known.

horus_khenty_irty.name: Horus of the two eyes

descriptions.default: A god stands beneath a pair of eyes: Horus Khenty-irty, "Horus foremost of the two eyes", one of the Seven Glorious Ones whom Anubis set to protect the sarcophagus of Osiris.

horus_khenty_irty.reference: Davis 1894; Stadler 2022 (Horus Mekhenti-irty); the translation "foremost of the two eyes" is unsourced

spirit_with_emblem.name: Spirit with a sign on his head

descriptions.default: A bearded god with a curled sign on his head: one of the Seven Glorious Ones, with the sons of Horus, who protect the sarcophagus of Osiris. Which of the Seven he is is not known.
A mummy-shaped god with a jackal's head: Duamutef, one of the four sons of Horus who protect the sarcophagus of Osiris.
A mummy-shaped god with a human head: Imsety, one of the four sons of Horus who protect the sarcophagus of Osiris.
A head rises from the top of a tall chest between the four sons of Horus. The chest may be the funeral chest of Osiris; the head may be the sun god's.
A mummy-shaped god with a baboon's head: Hapy, one of the four sons of Horus who protect the sarcophagus of Osiris.
A mummy-shaped god with a falcon's head: Qebehsenuef, one of the four sons of Horus who protect the sarcophagus of Osiris.
The great cow of the sky lies on a shrine, a flail on her back and a sun disc with plumes on her head. The dead man "sees the sun born of Yesterday above the thigh of the cow Mehurit."
The heading of the chapter continues: "about going out by day, about performing all the transformations in which one is pleased to be, about playing at draughts, about being in the sacred place."
A man raises one hand and holds up a small offering toward the great cow.
The wedjat eye rests on a shrine: the sacred Eye, made whole again after the fight of Horus with Seth.
A baboon squats facing the Eye of Horus. It is probably Thoth, who sets the Eye's hair in order and washes it when it weeps, giving back its life and health.

rosetau_gate.name: The gate

descriptions.default: A tall gate with a snake inside and three blades on its roof. The text names two gates here: the Gate of the Desert, through which Atum passes to the eastern horizon, and Rosetau. Which one is drawn is not known.

rosetau_gate.reference: TBP Spruch 17 (Backes: Tor der Wüste, Rasetjau); Davis 1894 (only the gate Atum passes through)

descriptions.default: Two figures kneel, each reaching a hand over a small pool: Heh, "Passing over Millions of Years", and Wadj-wer, the "Great Green". Their pools are the basin of natron and the basin of nitre, where the dead man is purified.

nephthys_kite.name: Nephthys as a kite

descriptions.default: Nephthys in the form of a kite, her sign of a basket on a house on her head, mourns at the head of the bier.

nephthys_kite.reference: Renouf & Naville 1904 (Isis and Nephthys as two kites); TBP Spruch 17 (lists kites, the Nephthys sign and the throne sign among this vignette's motifs)

mummy_on_bier.name: The mummy on the bier

descriptions.default: The mummy lies on a bier shaped like a lion, mourned by Isis and Nephthys as kites at its foot and head.

mummy_on_bier.reference: Renouf & Naville 1904 (Isis and Nephthys as two kites)

isis_kite.name: Isis as a kite

descriptions.default: Isis in the form of a kite, her throne sign on her head, mourns at the foot of the bier.

isis_kite.reference: Renouf & Naville 1904 (Isis and Nephthys as two kites); TBP Spruch 17 (lists kites, the Nephthys sign and the throne sign among this vignette's motifs)

descriptions.default: The Benu heron. "I am this great Bennou who is in Heliopolis": Osiris, whose body is the law of all that exists, of endless time and eternity.
The other lion of the horizon. "I am Yesterday and I know To-morrow": Tomorrow is Ra, who rises again each morning.
The sun disc between two hills: the horizon, where the sun sets and rises, between the lions of Yesterday and Tomorrow.

The heading of the chapter: "A chapter concerning the resurrection of the shades, about going out by day of the Netherworld, about being one of the retinue of Osiris, about feeding upon the loaves of the Good Being,"
One of the two lions that hold up the horizon. "Yesterday is Osiris," the text explains.
The sun boat sails with six gods standing in it, spears in hand. On a stand in the middle lies a crowned creature beneath the sun disc; what it is is not known.
A man holds up a small statue of Min (Khem) on his arm and presents a lotus flower to the dead man.
The dead man raises both hands in praise before the man who carries the statue of Min and the lotus.

A bird with a man's head and a god's beard stands on a low stand: the ba, the soul of the deceased, free to leave the tomb by day. It carries a djed, the sign of stability, and beside it stands the sign for the West.

falcon_on_perch.name: Sign of the West

descriptions.default: A falcon with a flail stands on a perch beside the ba: the sign for the West, the Amenti, the land of the dead.

falcon_on_perch.reference: "the sign for the West" is unsourced

senet_booth.name: The booth

descriptions.default: The deceased sits in a booth with his staff, before a small altar of loaves. The heading promises him the sacred place and a game of draughts (senet).

senet_booth.reference: Davis 1894; Stadler 2022 ("playing the senet game, sitting in a pavilion")

descriptions.default: The dead man stands with his staff, ready to set out: he goes out by day in any form he pleases.
